evidence.title: Lung Cancer Screening Delivery in a Decentralized Program: Patient and Provider Perspectives.
excerpts: IntroductionLung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death in Alabama, where screening uptake remains well below national benchmarks.

Decentralized screening programs, in which referring providers manage eligibility identification, referrals, and follow-up without dedicated coordination infrastructure, are common across clinical settings.
Yet the relationship between program design and delivery outcomes in decentralized contexts has received little attention.
This study examined how a decentralized lung cancer screening program delivered screening across each step of the pathway, from patient identification through annual follow-up.
Fifteen patients who had completed screening and six providers representing primary care, pulmonology, and radiology participated.
Interviews explored screening awareness, decision-making, and program delivery processes.
Transcripts were analyzed using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) and constant comparative method.
Reporting followed the COREQ guideline.ResultsDelivery failures were structural and concentrated at the front end of the screening pathway.
Eligibility identification depended on incidental patient exposure rather than systematic outreach.
Referrals reflected individual provider initiative rather than standardized workflows.
Result tracking and nodule follow-up fell to ordering providers without dedicated support.
Coverage gaps and geographic distance compounded these determinants.ConclusionReduced uptake in this decentralized program pointed largely to structural barriers.
Closing the implementation gap may require program design changes and proactive outreach that does not depend on the clinical encounter to begin.
Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in Alabama.
Screening with a low-dose CT scan can catch it early, when treatment is most effective.
Yet fewer than 6% of eligible people in the United States get screened, and rates in Alabama are even lower.
This study looked at how screening is delivered in practice.
We interviewed 15 patients and 6 healthcare providers at an Alabama medical center.
Patients ranged in age from 49 to 78.
Providers included primary care physicians, pulmonologists, and radiology staff.
Findings pointed to gaps in program infrastructure.
Eligibility identification relied on providers raising the topic during already full clinic visits.
Referrals depended on individual initiative.
Result tracking and follow-up fell to ordering providers working without dedicated tools or support.
Patients who reached screening often did so through persistence or chance.
Those with established provider relationships and consistent communication had a smoother experience.
Patients and providers were aligned on what would help.
Automated tools to flag eligible patients, a dedicated staff role to manage the process from start to finish, and outreach that reaches people before a clinic visit would each strengthen delivery.
These are changes at the program level, and participants described them as feasible and worthwhile.
The findings reframe the question.

evidence.title: Lumbar Facet Joint Morphology and Degenerative Lumbar Spondylolisthesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
excerpts: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science were searched through June 2026.
Studies evaluating lumbar facet morphology in adults with DLS were included.
Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed.
Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed.ResultsThirty-nine studies met the inclusion criteria.
Sixteen studies (3,321 participants) were included in the facet orientation meta-analysis.
Patients with DLS demonstrated more sagittally oriented facet joints than controls (SMD 1.30, 95% CI 0.78-1.82; p < 0.0001; I 2  = 97.2%).
Nine studies (1,913 participants) showed greater continuous facet tropism in DLS patients (MD 2.72°, 95% CI 2.07°-3.38°; p < 0.0001; I 2  = 47.2%).
Binary facet tropism was not statistically significant (OR 2.20, 95% CI 0.85-5.66; p = 0.0817).

Sex-specific, severity, and instability data were insufficient for quantitative synthesis.ConclusionDLS is associated with more sagittally oriented facet joints and greater continuous facet tropism than controls.
Limited sex-specific data and heterogeneity highlight the need for standardized measurement techniques and prospective longitudinal studies to clarify causality and sex-related effects.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence and Connected Technologies in Chronic Pain Management: A Scoping Review.
excerpts: Chronic pain affects over 1.5 billion people worldwide, facing persistent challenges in assessment subjectivity, treatment variability, and scalability (i.e., the limited ability to deliver individualized care to large populations within current clinical systems).
Artificial intelligence (AI) and connected health technologies have transitioned from experimental tools to clinical reality in pain management.
This scoping review maps current AI applications, identifies implementation gaps, and demonstrates the need for systematic technology integration in pain medicine.
We conducted a targeted literature search across PubMed, Scopus, MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Google Scholar.
From 487 identified articles, 23 met inclusion criteria for a detailed analysis.
A scoping review approach, following the Arksey and O'Malley framework, provided an integrative perspective on these rapidly evolving applications.
Notable applications include AI-guided spinal cord stimulation and wearable-integrated pain profiling.
Despite demonstrable clinical benefits across these domains, integration remains fragmented due to data governance challenges and educational gaps among practitioners.
AI is demonstrably improving chronic pain outcomes, yet integration remains fragmented due to data governance issues and educational gaps.
Professional societies must establish specialized AI committees, clinical guidelines, and structured training.
As this transformation occurs, pain specialists must lead this evolution rather than adapt reactively to external changes.

evidence.title: Predictors of Aggression in Children and Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
excerpts: Aggression is a common and impairing co-occurring behavior among children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), negatively affecting developmental outcomes, family functioning, and social participation.
Although numerous studies have examined factors associated with aggression in ASD, findings remain inconsistent, limiting efforts to improve early identification and intervention.
This systematic review synthesized current evidence on predictors of aggression in children and adolescents with ASD.
The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023416081).
A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library was conducted from database inception to 4 April 2024.
Eligible studies were evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute Checklist for cross-sectional designs and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies, and findings were narratively synthesized.
Thirteen studies met inclusion criteria and were of generally satisfactory methodological quality.
Across studies, six categories of predictors were identified: demographic, caregiver, core symptom, comorbidity, psychological, and biological factors.
Overall, aggression in ASD appears to arise from interacting individual, familial, and contextual influences.

These findings highlight the importance of assessing communication skills and sleep problems when evaluating aggression risk and suggest that interventions targeting these domains may reduce aggressive behavior.
Future research should employ longitudinal and cross-cultural designs to clarify developmental pathways and strengthen the evidence base for personalized intervention strategies.

evidence.title: Efficacy, Effectiveness, and Immunogenicity of the Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F Vaccine Administered During Pregnancy: Protocol for a Living Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
excerpts: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, with the highest burden in the first 6 months of life.
Maternal immunization with the bivalent (RSV-A and RSV-B) prefusion F (RSVPreF) protein subunit vaccine (ABRYSVO) is a recently recommended strategy for preventing RSV-related outcomes in infants.
This living systematic review and meta-analysis will synthesize emerging postlicensure data on the efficacy, effectiveness, and immunogenicity of the RSVPreF vaccine in real-world settings.
Primary objectives are evaluation of vaccine efficacy and effectiveness in preventing RSV-specific and all-cause respiratory disease and immunogenicity in infants and pregnant individuals.

Vaccine effectiveness outcomes include RSV laboratory-confirmed infection, RSV acute respiratory illness, RSV lower respiratory tract disease, RSV hospitalization, RSV complications, all-cause lower respiratory tract disease and hospitalization, and antibiotic use in infants with RSV infection.
Immunogenicity outcomes include maternal neutralizing antibody titers, maternal-infant transfer ratios, infant titers over time, and RSV viral load.

We will search MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, LILACS, Science Citation Index Expanded, Chinese biomedical and citation databases, clinical trial registries from January 2023 onward with no language restrictions, updating at least monthly.
Two investigators will independently select studies, extract data, and assess risk of bias.
Adjusted estimates will be standardized to vaccine efficacy and effectiveness.
Certainty will be graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) system.
This living systematic review was funded in June 2025.
Searches began in January 2023 and will continue with surveillance updates at least monthly until April 2028.
As of January 2026, 837 records were screened, 105 (12.5%) were assessed in full text, and 12 (1.4%) met the inclusion criteria, of which 10 (1.2%) contributed extractable data.
Data collection and analysis are ongoing and displayed on an interactive dashboard.
Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conferences, and a real-time dashboard, with the first effectiveness estimates available in July 2026.
This living systematic review and meta-analysis will provide a continuously updated synthesis of real-world evidence on maternal RSVPreF vaccination to inform clinical and policy decisions.

evidence.title: Efficacy and Safety of Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine for Depression With Anxiety and Somatic Symptoms: A Meta-Analysis.
excerpts: ObjectiveSomatic symptoms are often linked with depression and anxiety, making diagnosis difficult and limiting treatment effectiveness.
Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine has been studied as a complementary approach; however, its efficacy and safety have not been systematically evaluated.

This review and meta-analysis examined the effectiveness and safety of integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine in patients diagnosed with depression with or without comorbid anxiety and somatic symptoms.MethodsThis systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.
English-language studies published from 2014 to 2026 were searched in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus.
Randomized controlled trials comparing integrated therapy with control interventions were included.
The primary outcome was depression severity assessed by HAMD scores.
Secondary outcomes included anxiety symptoms, somatic symptoms, and adverse events.
A random-effects model was used, and heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2  statistic.ResultsEleven studies met review criteria.
Integrated therapy significantly reduced depression severity compared with the standard Western medicine control condition (MD = -3.95, 95% CI: -4.71 to -3.19; I 2  = 59%).
Anxiety symptoms were also significantly reduced (MD = -3.95, 95% CI: -4.65 to -3.26; I 2  = 50%).
Somatic symptoms, including sleep disturbances and pain-related outcomes, improved but were assessed descriptively because of reporting variability.
Adverse events were lower or similar in combined treatment groups, indicating a favorable safety profile.
However, given the methodological limitations, heterogeneity of comparator conditions, and low certainty of the available evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

evidence.title: A self-organized QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of English- and Turkish-associated EEG signals.
excerpts: Our primary aim is to develop an automated feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of EEG recordings acquired from English-speaking and Turkish-speaking participant cohorts.
Drawing inspiration from a quantum tunnel pattern called QTPat, we introduced a novel approach of dynamically generating directed graphs to extract textural features.
For our experiments, we utilized an EEG dataset containing 1652 English sentence-EEG pairs and 1600 Turkish sentence-EEG pairs.
These signals were recorded from 20 English-speaking and 20 Turkish subjects who were presented with standardized sentences in their respective native languages.
During the experiments, the participants were instructed to carefully contemplate each sentence while wearing a mobile brain cap system that acquired 14-channel EEG signals.
Our preprocessing pipeline involved subjecting the EEG signals to multiple filtered wavelet packet decompositions, using both 6 Daubechies and 6 symlet wavelet filters.
Subsequently, we extracted textural and statistical features employing the QTPat model, along with 20 statistical moments.
To enhance discriminative power, we applied neighborhood component analysis and the Chi2-function to select the most relevant features.
The k-nearest neighbor classifier was then employed to calculate predictive vectors.
To further refine the results, we introduced an iterative hard majority voting scheme, generating additional voted vectors.
Finally, we utilized a greedy algorithm to select the best-channel-wise and overall model results.
Using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO CV), the proposed framework achieved 96.37% classification accuracy using four selected EEG channels.
These findings demonstrate that the QTPat-based architecture can discriminate the two language-associated EEG cohorts under subject-independent evaluation.
However, because language and participant population are coupled in the available dataset, the present results should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of language-specific neural decoding.
Further studies using within-subject bilingual experimental designs are required to determine whether the identified EEG patterns specifically reflect language-related neural processing.

evidence.title: European Bioanalysis Forum cross-industry perspective on emerging small-molecule modalities: bioanalytical challenges and potential mitigation strategies.
excerpts: Emerging small molecule modalities, including oligonucleotides, peptides, lipid nanoparticles, covalent inhibitors and prodrugs, challenge conventional bioanalytical approaches.
Recognizing this, the European Bioanalysis Forum convened a cross-industry working group to systematically identify and categorize bioanalytical challenges across seven modality types.
Recurring issues include instability, poor recovery, matrix effects and anti-drug antibody interference.
Beyond documenting these challenges, the group collected preliminary mitigation strategies based on cross-company experience and scientific discussion.
These strategies represent potential approaches rather than formal recommendations.
The findings highlight that emerging modalities require early cross-functional assessment and modality-specific analytical strategies, guided by the intended use of the data.

This initial categorization provides a foundation for further scientific evaluation, community alignment and regulatory dialogue, supporting the development of science-driven, fit-for-purpose bioanalytical approaches as experience with these modalities evolves.

evidence.title: Major depressive disorder
excerpts: Major depressive disorder (MDD), also known as clinical depression, is a mental disorder characterized by at least two weeks of pervasive low mood, low self-esteem, and loss of interest or pleasure in normally enjoyable activities.

Introduced by a group of US clinicians in the mid-1970s, the term was adopted by the American Psychiatric Association for this symptom cluster under mood disorders in the 1980 version of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-III), and has become widely used since.
The disorder causes the second-most years lived with disability, after lower back pain.
The diagnosis of major depressive disorder is based on the person's experiences, and behavior reported by family or friends, and a mental status examination.
There is no laboratory test for the disorder, but blood testing and similar may be done to rule out physical conditions that can cause similar symptoms.
Men are much less likely to report than women, with approximately 33.2% of men and 43.0% of women with depressive symptoms reporting seeking help, possibly due to pressures of masking for men.
The course of the disorder varies widely, from one episode lasting months to a lifelong disorder with recurrent episodes.
Those with major depressive disorder are typically treated with psychotherapy and antidepressant medication.
While a mainstay of treatment, the clinical efficacy of antidepressants is controversial.
Hospitalization (which may be involuntary) may be necessary in cases with associated self-neglect or a significant risk of harm to self or others.
Major depressive disorder is believed to be caused by a combination of genetic, environmental, and psychological factors, with about 40% of the risk being genetic.
Risk factors include a family history of the condition, major life changes, childhood traumas, environmental lead exposure, certain medications, chronic health problems, and substance use disorders.

evidence.title: Endocannabinoid system
excerpts: The endocannabinoid system (ECS) is a biological system composed of endocannabinoids, which are neurotransmitters that bind to cannabinoid receptors, and cannabinoid receptor proteins that are expressed throughout the central nervous system (including the brain) and peripheral nervous system.
It is found in animals as simple as hydras, but absent in insects, who are hypothesized to have lost it due to a lack of arachidonic acid.

The ECS plays an important role in multiple aspects of neural functions, including the control of movement and motor coordination, learning and memory, emotion and motivation, addictive-like behavior and pain modulation, among others.
Two primary cannabinoid receptors have been identified: CB1, first cloned (or isolated) in 1990; and CB2, cloned in 1993.

CB1 receptors are found predominantly in the brain and nervous system, as well as in peripheral organs and tissues, and are the main molecular target of the fatty-acid neurotransmitter anandamide, as well as the most known active component of cannabis, tetrahydrocannabinol (THC).
Another endocannabinoid, 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG), also interacts with both CB receptors.
It is significantly more abundant in the mammalian brain than anandamide, exceeding it by two to three orders of magnitude.

The endocannabinoid system is sometimes called the endocannabinoidome or the expanded endocannabinoid system, as it includes a broader range of lipid mediators, receptors, and enzymes beyond CB1 and CB2.

evidence.title: Autism
excerpts: Autism, also known as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), is a condition characterized by impairment in social communication and interaction, as well as a need or strong preference for predictability and routine, sensory processing differences, focused interests, or repetitive behaviors.
Features of autism are present from early childhood and the condition typically persists throughout life.

Autism is classified as a neurodevelopmental disorder, and a diagnosis requires professional assessment that these characteristics cause significant challenges in daily life beyond what is expected given a person's age and social environment.
Because autism is a spectrum disorder, presentations vary and support needs range from minimal assistance to full-time, 24-hour care.
Autism diagnoses have risen since the 1990s, largely because of broader diagnostic criteria, greater awareness, and wider access to assessment.
The World Health Organization estimates that about 1 in 100 children were diagnosed between 2012 and 2021, noting an increasing trend.
Surveillance studies suggest a similar share of the adult population would meet diagnostic criteria if formally assessed.
Autism is highly heritable and involves many genes, while environmental factors appear to play a smaller, mainly prenatal role.
Boys are diagnosed several times more often than girls, with girls being better at hiding autistic traits.
Conditions such as anxiety, depression, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), epilepsy, as well as intellectual disability, are more common among autistic people.
Autistic people are also more likely to be a part of the LGBTQ community.
Certain savant abilities are also more common in autistic people than in other groups.

evidence.title: Timeline of aging research
excerpts: This timeline lists notable events in the history of research into senescence or biological aging, including the research and development of life extension methods, brain aging delay methods and rejuvenation.
People have long been interested in making their lives longer and healthier.
The most ancient Egyptian, Indian and Chinese books contain reasoning about aging.
Ancient Egyptians used garlic in large quantities to extend their lifespan.
370 BCE), in his Aphorisms, and Aristotle (384–322 BCE), in On youth and old age, expressed their opinions about reasons for old age and gave advice about lifestyle.
980 – 1037), known in the West as Avicenna, summarized the achievements of earlier generations about this issue.
